First, let's recall the secant-tangent identity:

$$
1+{tan}^{2}⁡x={sec}^{2}⁡x
$$

We rewrite the given expression using the secant-tangent identity as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}(1-{sec}^{2}⁡x)\cdot {cos}^{2}⁡x & =(1-(1+{tan}^{2}⁡x))\cdot {cos}^{2}⁡x \\  & =-{tan}^{2}⁡x\cdot {cos}^{2}⁡x\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we recall the following identity:

$$
\operatorname{tan}⁡x=\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}
$$

 

Using the above identity, we can further simplify our expression as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}-{tan}^{2}⁡x\cdot {cos}^{2}⁡x & =-\frac{{sin}^{2}⁡x}{{cos}^{2}⁡x}\cdot {cos}^{2}⁡x \\  & =-\frac{{sin}^{2}⁡x}{\cancel{{cos}^{2}⁡x}}\cdot \cancel{{cos}^{2}⁡x} \\  & =-{sin}^{2}⁡x\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
(1-{sec}^{2}\,x)\cdot {cos}^{2}⁡x=-{sin}^{2}⁡x.
$$
